chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > What this document is
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > What this document is]
A reference for the Dream11 account surfaces reached from the profile drawer. It describes what exists today, screen by screen. Read this if you are building anything that touches account identity, contact details, notification permissions, or account deletion.
Covered here: the account drawer and My Info & Settings. Documented elsewhere: How to Play / Fantasy Points (Scoring page). Balance and Withdrawal sit with Pri Chakrabarti. Help & Support is an open tracker row — see §4.
Sources: one native-resolution screen recording (718×1564, 5 Aug 2026) of My Info & Settings, plus PM confirmation from Anurag Sharma on deletion behaviour. Everything stated was directly observed or PM-confirmed; nothing inferred. Open questions are collected in §5.
Redaction: account-identifying values are replaced with [NAME], [USERNAME], +91 XXXXXXXXXX, and [name]@[domain].

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 1. The account drawer
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 1. The account drawer]
Every flow in this document is entered from the same place: a dark left slide-over that opens over Contest Home. It is the shared front door for account management. Its header is the user's avatar and username in caps ([USERNAME]) with a trailing chevron. Below it, items sit in three visually separated groups:
| Group | Items |
|---|---|
| Group 1 | My Balance · My Matches · My Vouchers · Subscriptions |
| Group 2 | My Info & Settings · How to Play · More |
| Group 3 | 24×7 Help & Support |
Below the groups, a More From Dream Sports shelf carries horizontally scrollable cross-sell cards: DreamStreet (Start Investing. Just Rs.10.), FanCode (Watch Live Sports), Dream Cricket 25 (#1 Cricket Game of India), and DreamSetGo (Sports Experiences).
The grouping is doing real work — money and activity in one group, account and reference in another, support isolated — so a new item cannot simply be appended without deciding which group it belongs to. The drawer mixes first-party navigation with cross-property promotion in one scroll. Neither recording opens More or the header chevron, so the contents of both are undocumented.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings]
The account's own record: who the user is, how they log in, and what they have consented to. Dark theme. The header carries a back control on the left and a ⋮ overflow on the right. Content is three cards, then a logout action outside the cards.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Personal Details
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Personal Details]
Two rows: Name ([NAME]) and Country (India). Neither row is editable. There is no Edit control, no tap affordance, and no explanation of where these values come from. For a real-money platform this is very likely deliberate — name and country have regulatory and payout consequences — but the screen does not say so. What Country actually drives, beyond display, is not established.
Identity mismatch: the drawer header shows [USERNAME], while Personal Details shows [NAME]. These are two different identity fields — a username/team name and a legal-style name — and only the second appears on this screen, read-only. Post-RL surfaces the first one as the team name on leaderboards, so it is the name opponents see. Where it is set, and whether a user can change it, is not established anywhere in these sources.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Login & Security
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Login & Security]
Two rows, each with an Edit pill: Phone Number (+91 XXXXXXXXXX) and Email ([name]@[domain]). This card is the only editable part of the screen, and both edits are gated behind OTP rather than saved directly.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Editing a phone number or email
chunks.h3: Editing a phone number or email
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Editing a phone number or email]
The edit pattern is inline. Tapping Edit replaces that row in place with an editable field and a GET OTP button directly beneath it. Phone: country flag, a non-editable +91 prefix, the editable number, and a clear (⊗) control; numeric keypad. Email: single text field with a clear control, plus two domain suggestion chips — @gmail.com and @yahoo.com; alphanumeric keyboard. Both fields are pre-filled with the current value.
Only one field can be in edit mode at a time. Opening the email editor collapsed the phone row back to its display state automatically.
The recording stops at GET OTP. Everything past that button — which number or address the code is sent to, what screen it opens, resend and timer behaviour, what a wrong code does, and whether a phone change has consequences for login or wallet — is undocumented. So is validation: no failure case was exercised, so there is no record of error copy for malformed input or for a number already registered to another account.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Permission
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Permission]
One row: Allow SMS notification, a toggle, observed on by default. The toggle flips immediately with no confirmation dialog and no visible toast. Whether the change persists on flip or on screen exit cannot be read off the recording, and which SMS category it governs — transactional, promotional, or both — is not established. This is the only permission on the account screen — there is no push, email, or WhatsApp equivalent.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Logout
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Logout]
A text action with an icon, positioned outside the cards at the bottom of the scroll. Not exercised, so whether it confirms before acting and where the user lands afterwards are both unrecorded.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Delete account
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > Delete account]
Reached from the header ⋮, and the most consequential path on the screen. Tapping it brings up a bottom sheet over dimmed content reading "Are you sure you want to delete your account? You'll lose all the progress you've made till now!" with two buttons: CANCEL (ghost) and DELETE (filled). CANCEL returns to the screen unchanged.
No intermediate menu appeared — the sheet slid up directly. So the ⋮ on this screen currently behaves as a single-purpose destructive control rather than a menu. The confirmation carries one warning, in general terms — and deletion is immediate and irreversible. There is no grace period, no ops review, no second confirmation, and no typed acknowledgement. From the account screen it is two taps to permanently destroy a real-money account. The copy does not mention the wallet balance or unsettled contest entries.
What happens to a wallet balance and to entries in contests that have not yet settled is not established, and neither is whether either acts as a hard block on deletion. Whether a deactivate-versus-delete distinction exists anywhere is also unrecorded.

chunks.heading_path: Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > What is not on this screen
chunks.h3: What is not on this screen
chunks.text:
[Account Management (AM) > 2. My Info & Settings > What is not on this screen]
There is no KYC or verification status, no PAN, no bank account or UPI detail, no address, no date of birth or state, no password or 2FA, no language setting, and no linked-accounts section. For a skill-gaming platform operating under Indian state-level restrictions, several of those must exist somewhere. The likely home is Balance / Withdrawal (Pri Chakrabarti), since payout is what forces verification — but that is a guess about placement, not a confirmed fact.

chunks.heading_path: AI Team Packs > What this document is
chunks.text:
[AI Team Packs > What this document is]
Knowledge base for AI Team Packs: one-tap generation of up to 20 diverse, DS-modelled fantasy teams drawn from a pre-generated pool and saved straight to My Teams. Read this if you are building anything that touches team creation entry points, the My Teams store, team caps, or DS-generated content. Sport: all cricket matches. Sources: [PRD] [Figma].
Shared rules referenced: R-01–R-06 (composition, enforced by DS at generation), R-07/R-08 (team caps), R-09 (no backups), R-12 (must complete before RL).

chunks.heading_path: AI Team Packs > 1. Purpose & user problem
chunks.text:
[AI Team Packs > 1. Purpose & user problem]
Post-F2P, the average user joins ~14 contests and manually builds ~13 teams per match — slow and repetitive. AI Team Packs generates many teams at once from a DS-modelled pool per match scenario. Segment served: multi-team creators.

chunks.heading_path: AI Team Packs > 2. How it works
chunks.text:
[AI Team Packs > 2. How it works]
DS pre-builds a pool of 3,000 teams per match scenario ahead of Round Lock, tagged by strategy. On request, the system randomly surfaces the requested count from that pool, filtered by the chosen strategy, and saves them directly.
User inputs ("Get Your Team Pack" sheet): Strategy (single-select): Mixed Pack (default), Team A heavy, Team B heavy, Batter heavy, Bowling heavy, Balanced. Mixed Pack = even spread across all combinations (e.g. 18 requested → ≥3 from each of 5 combinations, remainder random). Strategy names differ between PRD and Figma — GAP. Number of teams: static pills 20 / 10 / 5 / 1. Default 20 + Mixed Pack.

chunks.heading_path: AI Team Packs > 3. Business rules
chunks.text:
[AI Team Packs > 3. Business rules]
- Cap: 20 teams per generation call (R-08), independent of the 40-teams-per-match total (R-07). At 30 existing teams, a request for 20 saves 10.
- No backups — any generated team needing one is discarded (R-09)
- DS enforces player count, credit cap, C/VC and role limits at generation (R-01–R-05); DS also owns all post-lock team updates directly in its DB, with no app re-trigger
- Duplicates are discarded, the rest saved (R-06) — toast e.g. "8 eligible teams saved successfully"
- Cap-exceeded saves only up to the limit and reports the split — e.g. "19 eligible teams saved as team limit reached" / "19 of 20 teams created. 1 already existed"
- Generation must be ready as soon as the round is open (definition of "round open" is a Layer 0 open question)
- Available for all cricket matches

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > What this document is
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > What this document is]
A distillation of the Phase 1 PRD for Backups (a.k.a. Auto Substitutes): an optional step after team creation where a user pre-selects up to 4 substitute players so that, if a starter isn't in the final XI, the app auto-swaps a backup in at Round Lock. Read this if you are building anything that touches team composition after lock, the C&VC screen, My Teams cards, or Team Preview.
Sport: cricket only in Phase 1. Availability: all users, all tiers (confirmed 15 Sep 2026). Source: [PRD].
Shared rules referenced: R-01–R-06 (team composition), R-09 (max 4 backups), R-12 (edit window), R-14 (auto-sub at RL), R-31 (Firebase kill switch).

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 1. Why we're building this
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 1. Why we're building this]
Root problems: users lack the info/assistance to build a good team quickly and want all-playing players in it; people aren't around before Round Lock for odd-timing matches and miss the chance to edit; power users with many teams can't fix each one individually once lineups drop.
Solution: let users optionally pick backup players beyond the required 11. If a chosen starter isn't in the final XI, a backup is substituted automatically at Round Lock.

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 2. Objectives & success metrics
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 2. Objectives & success metrics]
| Goal | Metric | Target / hypothesis |
|---|---|---|
| Boost odd-hour participation | Odd-hour DAU participation | Improve % of DAU participating |
| Improve retention | Retention of users with non-playing players, with vs. without | Cut non-playing incidence 25% (8% → 6%) |
| Adoption | Adoption at match level | 50% |
| Usage | Usage among adopters | 50% of adopters use it in 60%+ of eligible matches |
Modelled impact: +0.43% PCJ annually. Validation data: ~8% of users have a non-playing player per match (~40% for new users); ~14% of DAU play odd-hour matches. Because the feature is a competitive advantage it can't be cleanly A/B tested at user level; it is evaluated via entry-point experiments (§7).

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 3. Scope (Phase 1)
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 3. Scope (Phase 1)]
- Optional backup selection alongside the main 11 (max 4 — R-09)
- Auto-replacement at Round Lock per the priority logic in §6 (R-14)
- Entry points: Create Team flow, My Teams, Team Preview
- Time-aware handling across pre-lineups, post-lineups, post-RL
- Cricket only, built to extend
- Everything behind a Firebase flag so all touchpoints can be killed centrally (R-31)

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 4. UX flow — Pre-lineups
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 4. UX flow — Pre-lineups]
Team creation is unchanged through the 11-player selection. Backups is an additional optional step after saving.
C&VC screen: before C&VC is picked, "Add Backups" is inactive (tap → error toast); Preview works as normal. Once C&VC is selected, "Add Backups Players" activates. Saving without backups continues the normal flow plus an educational toast. Entering the Backups flow means the team is already saved (confirmed via toast). Feature-education bottom sheet shows up to 3 times (not same-day), stopping once the user has used the feature or lineups are announced.
My Teams: an action icon (2nd position on the team card) is a persistent add/edit entry point; first three views also show a tooltip ("Select up to 4 Backups players").
Team Preview: no backups option during creation; during edits, backups show read-only unless entering from My Teams, which allows add/edit.
Selecting backups: manual selection mirrors team creation (same filters/sorting/stats) over all squad players not in the starting 11. No player-info page, no long-press. Deselecting (via '−' on image or name) shifts everyone below up one priority slot in real time. "Rules" (i) CTA opens a static page explaining swap logic. Reordering priority (long-press drag) is not P0; deferred past the March 2 release.
Team Preview from the Backups screen: backup names in a bottom bar (pills truncate at 69px). Exiting via 'X' asks for confirmation only if backups were actually added.
Editing backups pre-lineups: a backup who is added to the main 11 is auto-removed from backups (FE-only until save); count updates live. Dual-device edge case: editing the same team from two devices can cause save conflicts; PRD specifies an explicit error state (see source PRD for copy). Cloning: cloning a user's own team clones its backups.

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 5. UX flow — Post-lineups & Post-RL
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 5. UX flow — Post-lineups & Post-RL]
Post-lineups — entry points shrink because the goal (avoiding non-playing players) no longer applies the same way: Create Team has no C&VC entry point; Edit Team's C&VC entry point appears only if subs already added (Experiment 1 users only); My Teams promotional band disappears but the Teams Card icon stays; Team Preview add/edit entry point remains. Grouping (announced / backup / unannounced via green/purple/red dots) mirrors create-team grouping. Picking an announced substitute when backups already exist triggers a confirmation pop-up.
Post-RL, before swap: Team Preview shows a "Backups in review" banner for all teams while swap logic runs; the backups bar itself shows only for teams that used it. Team Compare is disabled (toast on tap). Player Stats carries a temporary disclaimer since selected-by% / C-by% reflect in-progress swaps.
Post-RL, after swap: swapped-in players get a green "subbed in" arrow; swapped-out players sit at the bottom with a red "subbed out" arrow. Expand arrow shows backups in (green, left) vs. players out (red, right). Team cards update to the post-swap WK/BAT/AR/BOWL split.

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 6. Auto-substitution logic (R-14)
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 6. Auto-substitution logic (R-14)]
Users assign priority across up to 4 backups. At Round Lock, players are pulled from the main 11 in this order:
1. Unannounced Captain
2. Unannounced Vice-Captain
3. Unannounced player (not C/VC), highest → lowest credits (+ tie-break)
4. Substitute-announced Captain
5. Substitute-announced Vice-Captain
6. Substitute-announced player, highest → lowest credits (+ tie-break)
Backups are applied in order: announced backups by priority, then substitute-announced backups by priority.
Key rules: replacements run sequentially until none remain; a swap that would violate team-creation rules (R-01–R-05) is skipped and the next eligible player is tried. If a C or VC is replaced, the highest-priority backup inherits the tag (R-05). A backup who was originally in the chosen 11 as a substitute pick is not replaced by another chosen backup. With multiple teams, replacements process in team-number order; if two teams would become identical after swaps, the higher-numbered team does not get the swap (R-06). If a swap would recreate an existing team, skip to the next team; after any swap, previously blocked swaps are re-evaluated.

chunks.heading_path: Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 7. Entry-point experimentation
chunks.text:
[Backups (Auto Substitutes) > 7. Entry-point experimentation]
Rolls out globally; the entry point is experimented on. Experiment 1: entry points on both the C&VC screen and My Teams — risk: distraction during creation, funnel impact. Experiment 2: My Teams only (persistent bar) — funnel-safe, likely lower adoption.

chunks.heading_path: Contests > What this document is
chunks.text:
[Contests > What this document is]
A reference for Dream11 contests: the types that exist, the variables that define one, how a user joins (and what ads they watch to do so), and what My Contests shows before Round Lock. [Contests > 1. Contest types]
Two Free-to-Play contest families:
1. Public contests — created and hosted by the platform. Special contests — larger, higher prize winnings. Public contests — up to 11 members, smaller prize winnings.
2. Private contests — created and hosted by Dream11 users; no prize winnings (R-11)

chunks.heading_path: Contests > 3. Contest join journey
chunks.text:
[Contests > 3. Contest join journey]
Joining a contest — public or private — is gated by rewarded ads for non-subscribers. Subscribers watch fewer or none. Ad unit: one rewarded ad, 15–120 seconds (R-24).
### Ad ladder
The number of ad units required per join steps up with how many contests the user has already joined in that match (scope confirmed 15 Sep 2026). Two bands: joins 1–10 and joins 11–40. The canonical table, including GAP cells for unconfirmed tiers, is Layer 0 Cross-cutting Rules §5. Earlier text on this page described three bands (1–10 / 11–20 / 21–40); that split is superseded.
### By tier
- Free: watches ads for every join; count per the ladder
- Pro: no ads for joins 1–10 in a match; ads from the 11th join. An upgrade bottom sheet fires before the 11th join's ad (R-26)
- Legend: no ads on any join

chunks.text:
[Contests > 4. My Contests (pre-Round Lock)]
Once a user joins a contest, an entry appears in their My Contests tab for that match, showing the contest and how many teams they joined it with. After Round Lock the same surface shows points, ranks and winnings — Post-RL §4.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > What this document is
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > What this document is]
A reference for how a Dream11 user gets help — what they can answer for themselves, what they can escalate, and what happens to a query once raised. Read this if you are building anything that touches user assistance: FAQ surfaces, help content, ticket raising, ticket history, or contextual help entry points. Not covered here: the money movement itself — deposits, withdrawals and balance mechanics sit with the Balance and Withdrawal flows.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 1. Where this sits
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 1. Where this sits]
Support is reached from the side menu, opened from the account avatar on Home. The row reads 24x7 Help & Support and sits at the bottom of the primary menu group. This is not the only way in — contextual entry points exist elsewhere in the product; the side-menu route is the canonical one.
### Ownership of the content
Help content and the query pipeline are managed in house. Queries raised through Write to Us escalate to internal CS teams. There is no third-party helpdesk vendor owning the taxonomy or the articles.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 2. Two presentation layers
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 2. Two presentation layers]
Support is one destination built from two layers. The native layer is the landing screen: Dream11's dark header chrome, instant render, standard app navigation. It holds the activity card and Most Asked Questions. The embedded layer is everything past the landing screen — Browse all topics, Past Tickets, and Write to Us. Each keeps the native dark header, but the content below is embedded, loads asynchronously behind a visible loader ("Setting up things for you…" for topics and Write to Us, "Loading…" for Past Tickets), and the help centre carries its own header and its own back control nested inside the native one.
### Why this matters when you build here
Every self-serve or assisted destination is behind a load state — perceived latency is a characteristic of this flow. The help centre has a second back stack — backing out of an article returns you within the help centre, not to the landing screen. Visual divergence is expected — the embedded layer renders light while the native shell is dark.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 3. The landing screen
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 3. The landing screen]
Four zones. Activity card: the top of the screen is given to money movement, not support activity. Its empty state reads No recent activity yet to show / All the activities related to deposits and withdrawals will be shown here. It surfaces the user's deposit and withdrawal history, not their tickets. Support opens by showing transactions because the overwhelming majority of people arriving here have a payment problem. Most Asked Questions: five questions, expandable in place. Browse all topics ›: entry to the help centre. View Past Tickets ›: entry to ticket history. Write to Us: prefixed by Didn't find what you were looking for? — positioned as the last resort.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 4. Most Asked Questions
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 4. Most Asked Questions]
Five questions, fixed order: 1. I haven't received my withdrawal money, what should I do? 2. I can't see my added money, what should I do? 3. I want to withdraw, how do I verify? 4. How do I withdraw my winnings? 5. How do I unlink PAN Card?
Tapping one opens a bottom sheet carrying the question as a heading, the answer as prose, a Was this helpful? row with thumbs up and down, and a close control. The answers are short and expectation-setting rather than diagnostic — e.g. withdrawals are usually immediate but can take up to three working days to reach a verified bank account. The list is not strictly static: it can change in response to the user having written in.
### The asymmetry worth knowing
All five questions are about money. None of the four browsable help topics is about money. Payment help exists in exactly two places: these five bottom sheets, and the CS queue. There is no browsable depth behind them.
### Helpful / not helpful
The reaction is saved. It does not change anything the user sees — no follow-up prompt, no escalation offer. Content-quality signal only.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 5. Browse all topics
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 5. Browse all topics]
The help centre. Reached behind the "Setting up things for you…" loader, under a Dream11 Support header with a sticky footer reading Can't find what you looking for? alongside a Contact Us button.
### The topic set
| Topic | Subtitle |
|---|---|
| Getting Started | What is Dream11, getting the app & more |
| Profile & Verification | View/Modify details, Verification & more |
| How to play | Create Teams, Join League & more |
| Watch Along & DreamBucks | Watch Along & DreamBucks |
Four topics, and this is the complete set.
### Three levels deep
Topic → Subsection → Article. Getting Started groups into About Us, Login & Registration, and Offers and Rewards. Profile & Verification groups into Managing My Profile / Account. An article is a full screen: the question as a coloured heading, then the answer as prose with light formatting. The subsection groupings are not visible from the topic list.
### Contact Us
The footer button persists across every level of the help centre and reaches the same Write to Us form. Ticket raising has two routes into one destination.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 6. Write to Us
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 6. Write to Us]
The only assisted channel. Reached from the landing screen, behind a loader.
### The form reveals itself progressively
On open, the form shows only the Issue Type field, plus a persistent amber note: Check for an acknowledgement sent to your email ID after raising the request. Selecting an issue type reveals the remainder of the form. The form's shape is a function of the issue type.
### Issue Type
A searchable select. Five options: Free To Play Winners · Account Verification or Changes · My Rewards and Offers · Withdrawals and TDS · My Matches and Leagues. This taxonomy does not mirror the help centre's four topics, and does not mirror the five Most Asked Questions. The product has three separate vocabularies for describing user problems.
### Fields revealed after selection
Observed under Free To Play Winners:
| Field | Required | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Issue Type | not asterisked | searchable select, five options |
| Preferred Language | yes | searchable select — English, Hindi, Marathi, Telugu |
| Match Name | yes | free text, placeholder Enter match name, example Ind vs Aus |
| Description | yes | multi-line |
| Attachments | no | one file only — .pdf, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .mp4, via Browse File |
| Submit | — | full-width |
Preferred Language carries the helper We will try our best to communicate with you in your preferred language. Issue Type is the one field without a required asterisk, despite the form being unusable until it is set. Match Name is mandatory under this issue type.
### Attachments
Browse File opens the OS picker: Photo Library, Take Photo or Video, Choose Files. Only one file can be attached; nothing warns the user before they try. No size cap is surfaced.
### Validation
Fires on submit, not on blur. Missing required fields turn red with a message beneath — Description is required. Errors appear together.
### After submit
The ticket appears in Past Tickets, and an acknowledgement is sent to the registered email. No SLA or turnaround time is shown or promised.

chunks.heading_path: CX — Help & Support > 7. Past Tickets
chunks.text:
[CX — Help & Support > 7. Past Tickets]
Ticket history, behind a loader. Empty state: You don't have any past ticket. Tickets raised through Write to Us appear here. Users can reply to and reopen past tickets, so this is a two-way surface. No turnaround expectation is displayed.

chunks.heading_path: Home & Navigation > 2. Top Nav
chunks.text:
[Home & Navigation > 2. Top Nav]
Four elements: Profile entry point, Dream11 logo, Subscriptions entry point, Notifications icon.
### Profile entry point
Tapping the profile icon (top left) opens the user's Dream11 profile, which holds: 1. Team name — changeable as many times as the user wishes. 2. Profile picture — changeable via a gallery upload flow. Amazon Rekognition screens uploads so offensive or explicit images cannot be set. 3. My Info & Settings entry point: Personal Details — not editable here; captured at login (Name, Country); Login & Security — editable (Phone number, Email); Permission — toggle for SMS notifications. Full My Info & Settings behaviour is in Account Management §2.
### Dream11 logo
Static.
### Subscription entry point
Three states, by subscription status: SUBSCRIBE — no active subscription; PRO — monthly Pro pack, or within a One Day Trial; LEGEND — monthly Legend pack. All three redirect to the Subscriptions page, where the user sees current status and can PURCHASE, CANCEL, RENEW or UPGRADE.
### Notifications icon
The bell (top right) opens the user's Notification Centre — the App Inbox, where all CleverTap-generated in-app notifications are served. Two notification types: without image, with image. Each carries a TTL and disappears when it expires.

chunks.heading_path: Home & Navigation > 3. Side Nav
chunks.text:
[Home & Navigation > 3. Side Nav]
Opened from the profile avatar. The drawer's structure — its three item groups, the More from Dream Sports cross-sell shelf, and design notes — is documented once in Account Management §1. This section only records what each item leads to.
### My Balance
Two sections: 1. Current cash balance (legacy, from RMG days) with the Winnings component specified; the user can withdraw cash winnings earned while operating. 2. My Prizes — summary page with total prize money earned and a match-by-match breakdown. Withdrawal mechanics are owned by Balance / Withdrawal (Pri).
### My Matches
Reached from the Side Nav or by scrolling to the end of the match pills list. Documented in Post-RL §3.
### My Vouchers
Reached from the Gift icon on Home or the Side Nav. Holds all vouchers received via brand targeting or bundled with a Subscriptions pack. Two layers: 1. Category — e.g. Dream Offers; copy is configurable. 2. Active / Inactive — by expiry date. Expired vouchers stay under Inactive for the retention window in R-16, then are removed.
### Subscriptions
Shows current subscription details for subscribers, or the packs available to buy. Full detail in Subscriptions.
### My Info & Settings
Review personal details; change contact details. Full detail in Account Management §2.
### How to Play
The fantasy rules reference — how to build a team, how points and ranks are calculated, how abandon works, prize distribution. Full detail in Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play.
### More
Static and informational links: Community Guidelines, Jobs, About Us, Terms & Conditions. No product logic; not documented further.
### 24×7 Help & Support
Full detail in CX — Help & Support.

Three things end simultaneously: 1. Team edits freeze — Create, Edit, Copy all disabled. 2. Contest joining closes. 3. Backup selection closes, and auto-substitution runs (Backups §6) — a team's post-RL composition can differ from what the user built.
One thing begins: the Scorecard appears (cricket only). DS also owns any post-lock updates to AI-generated teams directly in its DB; the app does not re-trigger.

chunks.text:
[L0.3 Match Lifecycle > 5. Live → Completed → Winners]

- Completed: final points written, leaderboard settles, Dream Team unlocks, result line appears on Scorecard.
- Winners: winners computed against the winnings template, ops approves, winnings released. Surfaces as "Won ₹X" under leaderboard usernames and "You won" on match cards. Not a separate screen.

chunks.text:
[L0.3 Match Lifecycle > 6. Variant: 2nd Innings]
A contest format that breaks the standard timeline. Documented only inside How to Play (Scoring §4); ownership unsettled.
- Lock is end of the innings break, not match start

chunks.heading_path: L0.1 Dream11 Overview & Free-to-Play Model > 1. What Dream11 is
chunks.text:
[L0.1 Dream11 Overview & Free-to-Play Model > 1. What Dream11 is]
Dream11 is a Free-to-Play fantasy sports app. Users build fantasy teams from the real squads of an upcoming match, join contests with those teams, and earn fantasy points based on how their players perform in the real match. Rankings within a contest determine prizes.
Cricket is the primary sport and the only one with full documentation today. Team-building rules, scorecards and the fantasy points reference are all cricket-only in current sources; other sports exist but are not yet documented.

chunks.heading_path: L0.1 Dream11 Overview & Free-to-Play Model > 2. The F2P model
chunks.text:
[L0.1 Dream11 Overview & Free-to-Play Model > 2. The F2P model]
Entry to every contest is ₹0. Prize pools still exist (e.g. Rank 1 wins ₹1 lakh in large public contests), so the platform funds prizes and pays for itself through two levers:
1. Ads — free users watch rewarded ads to join contests, with the ad load stepping up as they join more contests (see Cross-cutting Rules §5). Static ads (banners, masthead, voucher FAB) appear throughout.
2. Subscriptions — two tiers that remove ads and add benefits: Pro (₹99/month, list ₹199) — first 10 joins per match ad-free, static ads remain; Legend (₹399/month) — fully ad-free, plus FanCode streaming, multi-team join.
A third revenue track is direct deals — brand partnerships surfaced as vouchers in My Vouchers.
A legacy cash balance ("from RMG days") still exists in My Balance, with withdrawal of winnings handled by the Balance / Withdrawal flow.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > What this document is
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > What this document is]
A reference for the Dream11 experience after a match locks. It describes what exists today, screen by screen. Read this if you are building anything that touches a live or completed match: leaderboards, team previews, points display, comparison, or match scorecards. Not covered here: Withdrawal — sits with the Balance flow in Account Management.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 1. The shift at Round Lock
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 1. The shift at Round Lock]
Round Lock is the moment a match stops being editable. Before it, the user is preparing — creating teams, joining contests, setting backups. After it, the user is observing — watching points accrue, tracking rank, and eventually collecting winnings. Three things end at Round Lock: team edits, contest joining, and backup substitution windows.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 2. Match states
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 2. Match states]
A locked match moves through three states. The screens are the same across all three — same tabs, same layouts. What changes is how alive the data is and which affordances are present.
### Live
The match is in play. Points accumulate as the feed delivers ball-by-ball data. Points do not refresh on a timer. They update when the user refreshes or when a page loads. My Matches carries a refresh button for this. The header pill reads Live. Dream Team is unavailable — it appears only once the match is complete. Compare Teams is available, and works the same as post-match. The Scorecard shows live match status rather than a result.
### Completed
The match has ended. When the round is marked completed, final points are written and the leaderboard settles. The header pill reads Completed. Dream Team becomes available. The Scorecard shows a result line, for example SOB beat BPH by 12 runs.
### Winners
Winnings are declared. This follows Completed by a matter of minutes: final points are updated, winners are computed against the contest's prize breakup, operations approves the result, and winnings are released. Winners is not a separate screen. It surfaces as changes to existing ones — Won ₹X appears beneath usernames on the leaderboard, and the match card in My Matches shows You won.
### Why this matters when you build here
Because the layouts are near-identical, it is easy to assume a change applies uniformly across all three states. Dream Team's absence during Live is proof that element-level differences exist.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 3. Getting to a locked match
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 3. Getting to a locked match]
One path: Home → match carousel → "My Matches →" card (end of carousel) → My Matches (Upcoming / Live / Completed) → match row → Match screen with tabs MY CONTESTS (n) | TEAMS (n) | SCORECARD.
### Home
A horizontal carousel of match cards, each showing the two teams and a state pill. The final card is a My Matches → entry point.
### My Matches
Segmented into Upcoming / Live / Completed. Each row carries the format badge (T20, 100), the league name, both teams with logos, the date and start time, and a count line reading N Teams · N Contest. A refresh button appears during Live; a You won treatment appears once winnings are declared. Footer: Completed matches are shown for the last 7 days only (R-15).
### The match screen
Header shows a back control, both team logos, and the state pill. Three tabs:
| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| MY CONTESTS (n) | Contests the user joined for this match |
| TEAMS (n) | Every team the user created for this match |
| SCORECARD | The match scorecard |
TEAMS is match-scoped, not contest-scoped.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 4. My Contests
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 4. My Contests]
A list of the contests the user joined for this match. Each contest card shows the prize hook (Rank 1 Wins ₹1 LAKH) and, beneath it, a row per joined team with that team's points and current rank. Once winnings are declared, a You won treatment appears for winning entries. An advertising slot sits above the contest list; ad placement is owned by Monetization. Tapping a contest opens its detail, split into Prizes and Leaderboard.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 5. Prizes
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 5. Prizes]
Identical to the pre-Round-Lock prizes surface. The winnings template is set at contest creation and does not change after lock (R-29). The screen shows an ad slot, a three-column summary (Prize Pool ₹1.50 Lakhs · Spots 32,86,140 · Entry ₹0), then the rank-wise breakup: RANK 1 ₹1 LAKH; Rank 2 – 5,001 ₹10. Ranks are expressed as bands rather than individual rows.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 6. Leaderboard
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 6. Leaderboard]
The main Post-RL destination.
### Layout
A control row above the rankings: a count of participating teams as plain text (All Teams (32,86,140)), then two buttons — Compare and Dream Team. The count is display text only; there is no filter to narrow the leaderboard to the user's own entries.
### Rows
The user's own row is pinned to the top. Every row carries an avatar, username, team tag (T1, T16, T23), points, and rank. Winning rows also show Won ₹X in green beneath the username.
### Pagination and the 2,000-team cap
The leaderboard is paginated, and a maximum of 2,000 teams are shown (R-27). This is a deliberate cost control. In a contest with 32 lakh spots, the vast majority of entries are unreachable by scrolling. A user ranked #26,47,630 can see their own pinned row but cannot browse to their neighbourhood. Any feature premised on navigating to an arbitrary rank will not work.
### Ties and split winnings
Users on equal points share a rank, and the prize money for the positions they occupy is pooled and divided equally. The rank sequence then skips forward by the number of tied entries (R-28). Worked example:
| Points | Rank shown | Winnings each |
|---|---|---|
| 1,053.5 (two users) | #1 | ₹50,005 |
| 1,048.5 (five users) | #3 | ₹10 |
| 1,046.5 | #8 | ₹10 |
The two users tied at the top each received ₹50,005 — the Rank 1 prize of ₹1,00,000 plus one ₹10 second-place prize, split. The five users behind them all display as #3, and the next user appears at #8.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 7. Team preview
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 7. Team preview]
Reached by tapping any leaderboard row — the user's own or an opponent's. Header carries the team's identity (username and team number) and total points. Eleven players laid out on a cricket field, grouped by role: Wicket-keepers, Batters, All-rounders, Bowlers. Each player shows photo, name, points, and role badges — C for captain, VC for vice-captain, and a yellow DT shield for players who made the Dream Team. The preview is entirely read-only. No per-player breakdown of how a points total was assembled. Own team and opponent team previews are the same component. The DT shields let a user count how many of their picks made the Dream Team.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 8. Dream Team
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 8. Dream Team]
The best possible eleven for the match, reachable via the Dream Team button on the leaderboard. Same field layout as a team preview, with every player carrying a DT shield. It is match-level, not contest-level (R-23) — exactly one Dream Team per match. It is post-match only; during Live it is not shown.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 9. Compare Teams
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 9. Compare Teams]
The most intricate screen in this area.
### Entry is two-step
Compare is a mode: 1. Tap the Compare button on the leaderboard; the list dims. 2. Tap an opponent's row. Tapping an opponent's row without first tapping Compare opens their team preview instead.
### The comparison screen
Two teams side by side — the user's on the left, the opponent's on the right. Each side shows avatar, username, a team selector, and that team's rank. Both sides are selectable — dropdowns list all of the user's teams and all of the opponent's teams in that contest. Total points shown split across the two teams, with a margin line: Your opponent won by 416 pts. Exactly two teams can be compared at a time (R-30).
### The three sections
Always in this order, hidden when empty: 1. Different Players — players unique to each team, with a summary line quantifying which side's exclusive picks scored more. 2. Common Players with Different Caps — players both teams picked but with different captaincy, showing the multiplier arithmetic explicitly:
| Player | Left team | Right team |
|---|---|---|
| R Ahmed | 258 — captain, 129 ×2 | 193.5 — vice-captain, 129 ×1.5 |
| M Stoinis | 139 — no cap | 278 — captain, 139 ×2 |
| W Smeed | 91.5 — vice-captain, 61 ×1.5 | 61 — no cap |
This is the clearest explanation of C/VC economics anywhere in the product (R-19, R-20). 3. Common Players — identical picks with identical caps, shown with a flat total. Compare is available during Live as well as post-match.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 10. Fantasy Points System
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 10. Fantasy Points System]
Reached from the PTS icon on the Compare Teams header. This is the same component as How to Play in the account drawer — a CMS-driven webview, documented once in Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play. Content is organised by format — nine tabs: T20, OD, Test, T10, The Hundred, Other T20, Other OD, Other Test, Sixes (a snapshot; the tab set is CMS content). Whether a sport-level selector sits above the format tabs is unresolved. Scoring rules differ by format (R-22): a wicket is +30 under T20, +20 under Test, +16 under Other Test. Anyone building against fantasy points should not assume a single scoring table exists, or that the format list is fixed.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 11. Teams
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 11. Teams]
Every team the user created for the match, regardless of contest. Each team is a card showing team name and number (JJQRXD ALPHAS (T1)), total points, captain and vice-captain, and the role split — WK 2 · BAT 3 · AR 4 · BOWL 2. Worked set from one match: T1 632.5, T2 740, T3 511, T4 607, T5 432. Tapping a card opens the read-only team preview. An ad slot sits at the top.

chunks.heading_path: Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 12. Scorecard
chunks.text:
[Post RL — Leaderboard & Winnings > 12. Scorecard]
The real match scorecard, fed by the same data that drives fantasy points. It does not exist before Round Lock. It supports cricket only.
### Structure
A status band shows the result once complete or live status while in play. A dismissible note reads Players in your team are highlighted in blue, followed by a horizontally scrollable row of chips, one per team the user built, ordered by points descending. Selecting a chip changes which team's players are highlighted. Innings are collapsible accordions with team, innings number, and score (SOB INN 1 — 128-8 (100)). An expanded innings contains: Batting table (R / B / 4s / 6s, dismissal beneath name), Extras, Total, Did not bat, Bowling table (B / R / W). Blue highlighting marks team membership only — captains and vice-captains are not distinguished.
### Feed divergence
Both the scorecard and fantasy points derive from the same feed, and the feed can lag the real match. The scorecard can therefore differ from the actual match state at a given moment. This is a known characteristic rather than a defect, and it explains a recurring class of user confusion during live matches.

The reference for how Dream11 explains fantasy scoring to users: the How to Play / Fantasy Points surface. It is one component reached from two places — the account drawer (as How to Play) and the PTS icon on the Compare Teams header post-RL (as Fantasy Points System). A change here lands in both. Read this if you are building anything that touches scoring copy, format tabs, the CMS that publishes them, or any screen that explains why a team scored what it did.

Shared rules referenced: R-19 (Captain 2×), R-20 (VC 1.5×), R-21 (lineup bonus +4), R-22 (scoring varies by format, CMS-driven).

chunks.page: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play
chunks.heading_path: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 1. It is a webview, and the content is CMS-driven
chunks.h2: 1. It is a webview, and the content is CMS-driven
chunks.text:
[Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 1. It is a webview, and the content is CMS-driven]
How to Play is a webview whose content is CMS-driven. It can change without an app release. The theming is the visible tell — light background, navy and dark-maroon text, pill tabs, green values, red outlined badges — inside an app that is otherwise dark.
This determines who changes scoring copy and how fast: scoring copy and values are not gated on releases — a rule change can ship the same day, so can a mistake; the format tab set is content, not code — formats can appear or disappear without anyone touching the app; content ownership sits outside the app team — whoever publishes to the CMS owns what the product says about scoring; native assumptions do not hold — deep links, native instrumentation and native theming all need checking.

chunks.page: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play
chunks.heading_path: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 2. Format tabs
chunks.text:
[Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 2. Format tabs]
A horizontally scrollable strip of pills, in this order: T20 · OD · Test · T10 · The Hundred · Other T20 · Other OD · Other Test · Sixes. T20 is selected by default. Later tabs sit off-screen until scrolled, so Sixes is not visible on arrival.
Switching tabs changes two things: 1. The values change — scoring differs materially by format. 2. The available sections change — New Fantasy Formats appeared only under T20; every other format showed Fantasy Points and Other Important Points only. A section can be absent entirely for a given format, and which formats carry which sections is itself CMS content.
Sixes is not a cricket match length in the way the others are. Its scoring is built on Consecutive Boundary and Consecutive Six, which suggests a distinct game mode.

chunks.page: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play
chunks.heading_path: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 3. Fantasy Points section
chunks.text:
[Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 3. Fantasy Points section]
Expanded by default, with a PTS icon on its header. Two treatments inside.
### Important Fantasy Points
An always-visible, non-collapsible card under a green label — the highest-impact rules surfaced without a tap. Three rows for most formats, four for The Hundred. A red-outlined New badge marks recently changed rules. As observed on 5 Aug 2026:
| Format | Important Fantasy Points |
|---|---|
| T20 | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) New +30 · Run +1 · Dot Ball +1 |
| OD | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) New +30 · Run +1 · Dot Ball (Every 3 dot balls) +1 |
| Test | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) +20 · Run +1 · Catch +8 |
| T10 | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) New +30 · Run +1 · Dot Ball +1 |
| The Hundred | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) +30 · Run +1 · Catch +8 · Dot Ball New +1 |
| Other T20 | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) New +30 · Run +1 · Catch +8 |
| Other OD | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) New +30 · Run +1 · Catch +8 |
| Other Test | Wicket (Excluding Run Out) +16 · Run +1 · Catch +8 |
| Sixes | Consecutive Boundary +2 · Consecutive Six +3 · Dot Ball +1 |
This table is evidence, not the source of truth. A wicket is +30, +20 or +16 depending on the tab, and even the set of highlighted events differs. Because the content is CMS-driven it can change without a release. The app is authoritative for current values.
### Sub-accordions
Beneath the card: Batting, Bowling, Fielding, Additional Points. Single-open — expanding one collapses the others. T20 as a worked example:
| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| Batting | Run +1 · Boundary Bonus +4 · Six Bonus +6 · 25/50/75/100 Run Bonus +4/+8/+12/+16 · Dismissal For A Duck −2 · Strike Rate (Except Bowler) Points |
| Bowling | Dot Ball +1 · Wicket (Excluding Run Out) +30 · Bonus (LBW/Bowled) +8 · 3/4/5 Wicket Bonus +4/+8/+12 · Maiden Over +12 · Economy Rate Points |
| Fielding | Catch +8 · 3 Catch Bonus +4 · Stumping +12 · Run Out (Direct Hit) +12 · Run Out (Not A Direct Hit) +6 |
| Additional Points | Captain Points 2× · Vice-Captain Points 1.5× · In Announced Lineups +4 · Playing Substitute +4 |
Additional Points is the section to know. It holds the C/VC multipliers (R-19, R-20) and lineup bonuses (R-21) — the rules that drive most of the points spread between two similar teams, and the ones Post-RL's Compare Teams screen exists to explain. It is also the least discoverable, sitting last behind a collapsed header. A few rows carry an inline chevron for a third disclosure level — Bonus (LBW/Bowled), Consecutive Boundary, Consecutive Six. None were opened; contents unrecorded.

chunks.heading_path: Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 4. New Fantasy Formats — 2nd Innings
chunks.text:
[Scoring — Fantasy Points / How to Play > 4. New Fantasy Formats — 2nd Innings]
Observed only under T20. A single prose block headed 2nd Innings, documenting a distinct contest format:
- Any 5 players — no role or squad minimum conditions
- Contest locks at the end of the innings break, before the first ball of the 2nd innings
- Ranks determined on 2nd-innings points only
- Announced-lineup points are not awarded
- Early Start Protocol — if the 2nd innings starts before the set deadline: more than 2 overs bowled → contest abandoned; 2 overs or fewer → contest and winner declaration proceed as scheduled
This is a real product mechanic with its own lock timing, team-building rules and abandonment logic — and the only place it is described to the user is inside a collapsed accordion in a help screen. Anyone working on Contest Join, team validation or Round Lock needs to know it exists: Round Lock is not match start, teams are 5 not 11, role minimums do not apply. Ownership unsettled.

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Subscriptions Construct
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Subscriptions Construct]
There are two subscription types: Pro — Rs.99 per month with limited benefits; Legend — Rs.399 per month with bigger benefits. This is the standard pricing. To more price sensitive cohorts, we will do differential pricing to nudge them to purchase either Pro or Legend.

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Subscription Benefits
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Subscription Benefits]
### Pro Tier
1. 10 teams per Contest Join will be ads free, from the 11th team onwards the user will need to watch 1 ad per contest join (CJ). The user will continue to see all banner ads on the platform. (Note: per-tier ad counts beyond the 10th join are under review — see Layer 0 Rules §5.)
2. The user will also receive a Rs.1000 off DreamSetGo voucher
3. The user will also receive 20 Dream Cricket gems — DSG vouchers as part of their monthly subscription each month
4. The user will continue to see static ads [banners, masthead, voucher fab]
### Legend Tier
1. All 40 teams per match will be ads free
2. The user will also not see any static ads [banner, masthead, voucher fab]
3. FC live streaming monthly pass — for ALL sports available via FC — viewable on the leaderboard for those matches for which a fantasy contest is available
4. The user will also receive Dream Cricket + DSG vouchers as part of their monthly subscription each month
5. Team backups — NOTE: incorrect; Backups is available to all users (R-09, resolved 15 Sep 2026). Line retained pending page cleanup.
6. The user will also have multi team join flow available [ability to join multiple teams in one shot]

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Buying a Subscription
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Buying a Subscription]
The user can buy a subscription by clicking on SUBSCRIBE from the top NAV, or clicking on the Subscriptions CTA from the side NAV. Both lead to the Subscriptions page, which shows: Page Header giving the main value — Ads Free, Vouchers & Premium Features.
Pack 1: Legend [Rs.499 slashed to Rs.399]. All the benefits of Legend broken down by offering Company: Dream11: Ads Free; FanCode: LiveStreaming; Dream Cricket: Gems; DreamSetGo: Discount Voucher.
Pack 2: Pro [Rs.199 slashed to Rs.99]. All the benefits of Pro broken down by offering Company: Dream11: Ads Free (up to 10 joins per contest); Dream Cricket: Gems; DreamSetGo: Discount Voucher. FanCode live streaming is a Legend-only benefit and does not appear in the Pro breakdown.
The Pro Pack also offers a One Day Trial — the user can try Ads free for just one day. No vouchers which are part of the Pro pack will be disseminated to users who opt in for the One Day Trial. Every user can avail their One Day Trial only once. Once they opt in, for the next 24 hours, they will not see any ads up to 10 joins per contest. At the end of the 24 hour period, they return to being a non subscribed user (R-18).

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Upgrading a Subscription
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Upgrading a Subscription]
A user can upgrade from Pro to Legend from 2 touch points: 1. Subscriptions page — the Legend pack is right below their own MANAGE SUBSCRIPTIONS component. 2. Upgrade bottomsheet which comes contextually right before the ad for their 11th join happens. This bottomsheet tells the user that they have run out of credits and to Upgrade to Legend which is fully Ads free (R-26).

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Downgrading a Subscription
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Downgrading a Subscription]
This is when a user downgrades from Legend to Pro. 1. A user can cancel their Legend subscription; as part of this flow they can be nudged to switch to Pro instead. Their Legend renewal is cancelled but they still enjoy Legend benefits until the end of the original cycle. At the end of this cycle, their mandate for Pro begins — they are charged for Pro and the new cycle has Pro benefits only. 2. A user can cancel, wait a few days and then directly purchase Pro. Same treatment: Legend cycle completes, then they move to Pro. The actual payment is taken at the end of the cycle, so the user can reverse their action until then and cancel the mandate (R-17).

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Cancelling a Subscription
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Cancelling a Subscription]
1. In app flow: MANAGE SUBSCRIPTION → CANCEL CTA, which takes the user outside the app to the Google Play Store or App Store where the final cancellation takes place. 2. Outside app flow: the user goes directly to the Play Store or App Store and cancels there; on returning to Dream11 they see their updated status immediately. In both cases the final cancellation can only be done on the Play Store / App Store side, with Dream11 reflecting the change (R-17).

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Renewing a Subscription
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Renewing a Subscription]
Once a subscription has been cancelled, a RENEW CTA appears on top of MANAGE SUBSCRIPTIONS. Clicking it takes the user to the Play Store / App Store to restart. Renewing while the previous cycle is still active maintains the same cycle date. Renewing while the current cycle is inactive restarts the cycle from the date of renewal — it mimics a first-time purchase.

chunks.heading_path: Subscriptions > Subscription Vouchers
chunks.text:
[Subscriptions > Subscription Vouchers]
Vouchers are given to users at the point where their subscription renews every month. When a user upgrades from Pro to Legend, they receive the Legend vouchers immediately. One Day Trial users do not receive vouchers. Vouchers are shown in My Vouchers under Active until they expire, after which they move to Inactive (R-16).

chunks.text:
[Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > What this document is]
Reference for the three manual team-building flows: Create Team, Edit Team and Copy Team. Everything a user does to a team by hand, before Round Lock. Sport: cricket (rules for other sports not documented). Sources: [Recording] [PRD].
Sub-features with their own pages: Backups (Auto Substitutes), AI Team Packs, Guru Teams (planned).
Shared rules: all team-composition constraints (11 players, 100 credits, min per team/role, one C and one VC, duplicate check, 40-team cap) are defined once as R-01–R-07 in Cross-cutting Rules. The Round Lock freeze is R-12. This page cites those IDs rather than restating values.

chunks.heading_path: Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > 1. Create Team
chunks.text:
[Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > 1. Create Team]
### 1.1 Feature definition
Manual team-building flow: select 11 players from the match squad, assign Captain / Vice-Captain, save a new team in a round.
### 1.2 Purpose
A user must have at least one team to join any contest.
### 1.3 Flow-specific rules & logic
- Entry points: Contest page → Create Team; also from the Teams tab
- Screen sequence: Squad selection (role tabs ALL / WK / BAT / AR / BOWL; each row shows % selected by others + credit cost) → Select C & VC (legend C = 2×, VC = 1.5×; rows show % of others who picked each as C/VC) → Preview Lineup (shows credits, not points) → Save
- The Team Pack button on this screen is an entry point into AI Team Packs, not a separate feature
- After Save, user lands on Contest page → Teams tab; the new card shows a WK/BAT/AR/BOWL split
- Post-save tip: "Add Backups to (Team) to replace unannounced and substitute players" — surfaces Backups as the next step
- Validation enforced: R-01, R-02, R-03, R-04, R-05. Duplicate check R-06 — whether it fires at Create is a GAP
### 1.4 Dependencies
Round-specific player pool · credit & roster validation engine · Round Lock timer · AI Team Packs (via Team Pack entry) · Backups (via post-save tip)
### 1.5 Known limitations & gaps
- Error copy for credit-exceeded / role-minimum states not observed — GAP
- Whether R-06 applies at Create, not just Copy — GAP

chunks.heading_path: Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > 2. Edit Team
chunks.text:
[Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > 2. Edit Team]
### 2.1 Feature definition
Modify an existing team's players and/or C/VC before Round Lock. Same team ID is retained; no new team is created.
### 2.2 Purpose
Users revise teams as information arrives — toss, lineups, unannounced players — and want the contests they already joined to carry the revised team.
### 2.3 Flow-specific rules & logic
- Entry: edit (pencil) icon on a team card in the Teams tab
- Opens the squad-selection screen pre-loaded with the existing 11; same downstream steps as Create
- Editing can change role composition (observed BAT 1→2, AR 5→4); team ID/number retained
- Contests already joined with the team are automatically joined with the edited version
- Available until Round Lock; fully frozen after (R-12)
- Editing a team with backups: see Backups §4
### 2.4 Dependencies
Same as Create, plus an existing saved team.
### 2.5 User behaviour
Most used after lineups are announced, typically 30–45 min before Round Lock.

chunks.heading_path: Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > 3. Copy Team
chunks.text:
[Teams — Create, Edit & Copy > 3. Copy Team]
### 3.1 Feature definition
Create a new team pre-filled with an existing team's 11 players, to modify and save as a distinct team.
### 3.2 Purpose
Faster than starting from scratch when a user wants a variant of a team they already built.
### 3.3 Flow-specific rules & logic
- Entry: copy icon on a team card — cards carry exactly two icons, edit and copy; no delete, no share
- Opens Create Team pre-filled with all 11 players; user can change players and C/VC → Save
- Save is blocked if the result is identical (players + C/VC) to a saved team — R-06
- Copy is within the same round only
- Copying the user's own team also copies its backups (Backups §4)
### 3.4 Dependencies
Same as Create, plus a source team.
